message:
test(build): catch a target registered without its source

Test 1, build 1.

Five commits in this branch do not configure: 7dd0ffc, a236e1e, cc21ff4, 8d01995 and b941f28.
CMakeLists registered remote60_host_two_dispatcher_e2e_test while I deliberately kept the source
uncommitted, so a clean checkout at any of them dies at the generate step with "Cannot find source
file" and the whole native_poc build is unavailable. 461b753 fixed it by adding the source, and the
current tip configures from an empty directory -- verified, exit 0 with zero CMake errors.

It built for me the entire time. The file was sitting in my working directory, so every build I ran
succeeded and every build anyone else ran failed. A reviewer checking out a fixed hash is the only
way that gets noticed, and that is how it was.

The suggested fix -- drop the registration in a follow-up -- was right when it was written and is
wrong now: the source exists at HEAD, so removing the block would delete working coverage rather
than repair anything. The five broken commits stay broken; history is what happened, the reviewer
has already verified hashes in that range, and rewriting it to look tidy would invalidate their
work to hide mine.

What is worth having is the check. It reads CMakeLists, pulls out every path under src/ or tools/,
and asserts the file exists -- 518 entries today. Removing the same source reproduces the failure
and names it. Generated sources under the binary directory are skipped, since they do not exist
until the build makes them.

It also asserts the scan found something, because a parser that matches nothing reports a clean
bill forever. That is the third time in this task a scan needed proof it could see anything before
its silence counted for something -- the shipped-helper gate needed it twice.

What it does not cover: a missing include directory, a target linking a library nobody provided,
anything else configure would object to. It covers the one mistake that is invisible locally, which
is the one that got made.
